title: Independent and Joint Prospective Associations of Screen Time and Sleep Disturbance with Body Mass Index and Waist Circumference Among U.S. Adolescents
authors: Al-Shoaibi AA, Helmer CK, Shim J, Choi W, Dooley EE, Gooding HC, Pettee Gabriel K, Baker FC, Nagata JM

primary_models.name: Weighted multivariable linear regression of year-2 BMI and waist circumference on baseline socializing screen time (texting + video chat + social media), adjusted for baseline BMI/WC and sociodemographics
primary_models.location_in_paper: Supplementary Tables S6 (BMI) and S7 (WC), referenced in Results p. 6 ("Supplementary Tables S6 and S7 show the associations of specific screen time modalities with BMI and WC, with results consistent with the main findings"); subtype analysis described in Statistical Analysis p. 4. The supplementary appendix is NOT bundled in the PDF on file (author manuscript, 20 pages), so no estimates could be copied.
primary_models.design: Prospective longitudinal cohort. Screen time (including the socializing subtype) is measured once at ABCD baseline (2016-2018); BMI and WC are measured at baseline and at the year-2 follow-up. The DV is a single follow-up value (year-2 BMI or year-2 WC), with the baseline value of the same anthropometric measure entered as a covariate, so the coefficient reflects association with year-2 adiposity net of baseline adiposity. No repeated measures. Interaction terms between screen time and sleep were tested and reported as nonsignificant (p. 4); whether the subtype models were also sex-stratified cannot be determined without the supplement.
primary_models.sample: ABCD Study (release not stated in the manuscript). N = 7,445 participants with complete baseline screen time, sleep disturbance and sleep duration data and year-2 BMI and WC (COVID-19 reduced year-2 anthropometric collection; Supplementary Table S1 compares included and excluded participants). Implausible anthropometric values excluded (BMI z <= -4 or >= 8 SD; WC z < -4 or > 4 SD). Remaining missing covariate data handled by multiple imputation by chained equations (Supplementary Data S4). Age 9-10 at baseline, mean 9.9 (SD 0.6); 3,511 females (47.3%) and 3,934 males. Weighted race/ethnicity: 5.9% Asian, 16.6% Black, 16.2% Latino/Hispanic, 3.5% Native American, 56.5% White, 1.3% Other. 57.0% household income < $75,000; 85.3% parent with college education or more (Table 1, p. 17).
primary_models.iv: Baseline socializing screen time, one of three screen time subtypes (TV shows/movies, video games, socializing) derived from the ABCD Youth Screen Time Survey (p. 3). Socializing is defined by the authors as texting, video chatting, and social media, so it is built exclusively from phone/SM items and qualifies under FT-IC2. Total screen time was a weighted average of typical weekday and weekend day hours; the manuscript does not state whether the socializing subtype was entered as continuous hours/day or categorized, and no descriptive statistics for socializing time are given in the main text (Table 1 reports only total daily screen time, mean 3.7 h, SD 2.9). Units and coding must be confirmed from Supplementary Tables S6/S7.
primary_models.dv: Two continuous outcomes at the year-2 follow-up, modeled separately: (1) BMI (kg/m^2), computed from the mean of three measured weights and heights; year-2 mean 20.6 (SD 4.9); (2) waist circumference (units not stated in the manuscript; presumably inches per the ABCD protocol), mean of two measurements; year-2 mean 28.8 (SD 4.9) (Table 1, p. 17).

primary_models.equation: Y2_outcome[i] = b0 + b1*socializing_screen_time[i] + b2*baseline_outcome[i] + b3*age + b4*sex + b5..b9*race_ethnicity + b10..b15*income + b16*parent_ed + b17*physical_activity + b18..*study_site + b..*pubertal_status + e[i], where Y2_outcome is year-2 BMI or year-2 WC (separate models). Whether other screen subtypes and sleep variables also enter is not stated for the subtype models.
primary_models.estimation: Weighted multivariable linear regression in Stata 18, with American Community Survey-derived sampling weights to account for complex design and nonresponse (Supplementary Data S5). Missing data imputed with multiple imputation by chained equations. Regression assumptions reported as tested and met. alpha = 0.05; no multiple-comparison correction reported. Main models also stratified by sex; whether S6/S7 present sex-stratified subtype estimates is unknown. Sensitivity analyses using complete-case data (Supplementary Tables S8-S13) reported as yielding comparable findings; it is not stated whether these include subtype models.

Screen time x sleep interaction terms
excluded_models.why: Reported only as nonsignificant; no coefficients printed, and they involve total screen time, not a phone/SM variable.

d_transformation.native_metric: B (unstandardized linear regression coefficient), assumed from the main-table format; to be confirmed in Supplementary Tables S6/S7
d_transformation.conversion_formula: beta_std = B * SD_IV / SD_DV; d = 2 * beta_std / sqrt(1 - beta_std^2) (Borenstein et al. 2009 eq 7.1). If socializing is instead categorized (e.g., high vs. low group), d = B / SD_DV (adjusted group difference over pooled SD) would apply.
d_transformation.contrast_type: Unknown until the supplement is read: per 1 hour/day of socializing screen time if continuous, or category vs. reference if categorized.
d_transformation.notes: Not transformable with the material on file because the socializing estimates themselves (Supplementary Tables S6/S7) are not in the PDF. SD_DV is available from Table 1 (p. 17): year-2 BMI SD 4.9, year-2 WC SD 4.9 (weighted analytic sample, n = 7,445). SD_IV for socializing hours is not reported in the main text; it may appear in the supplement. Once the supplementary appendix is obtained, this paper should become transformable if B, its CI, and an SD for socializing time are reported.

extraction_flags: The PDF on file is the right paper: the PMC author manuscript of Al-Shoaibi et al. 2025, Child Obesity, 20 pages. It does not include the supplementary appendix. The only phone/SM analysis is the "socializing" screen-time subtype (texting + video chat + social media) regressed on year-2 BMI and WC, and its numbers are only in Supplementary Tables S6 and S7. I could not get that appendix. Europe PMC says the article is not open access. The PMC file (PMC12320422, NIHMS2098192-supplement-supplementary_appendix.docx) is behind a proof-of-work bot-check page, and I did not try to get past it. So the M1 card has the full model spec taken from the main text (Methods p. 4, Table 2/3 footnotes, Table 1), but both estimate cells (BMI, WC) are null placeholders. n_estimates is 0. A human needs to download the appendix by hand, add it to the repo, and fill in B/CI/p for socializing. They should also check: (1) whether socializing was continuous hours/day or categorized; (2) whether the three subtypes were entered together or in separate models; (3) whether S6/S7 are sex-stratified (if so, add Female/Male cells or columns); (4) whether an SD for socializing time is reported, which is needed for d; (5) whether the S8-S13 complete-case tables include the subtypes. SD_DV is taken from Table 1: year-2 BMI SD 4.9, year-2 WC SD 4.9. WC units are not stated in the manuscript. The Discussion says TV/movies and video games were "particularly associated", which suggests socializing was weaker or null. Covariate lists differ a little: Table 2/3 footnotes include pubertal status, but the Figure 1-4 captions leave it out. The ABCD data release is not stated. The draft overwrote an earlier paper_215.json in docs/data/drafts.
